title: Setting a workspace up
message: Nine steps, in order; each unlocks the next. A key so the AI works, then the accounts you publish to.
audience: Admins setting up a new company workspace

scenes.headline: Setting a workspace *up.*
scenes.sub: Keys, connections, and the order that unlocks the rest.
scenes.narration: A workspace is one company. Its keys, accounts, voice, slots and content are its own, invisible to every other workspace. This video walks the setup once, in order, because each step unlocks the next. Before you start, check the workspace switcher at the top left.

scenes.headline: No key means placeholder *text.*
scenes.narration: Step one: give it a brain. Settings, then Keys. Paste an AI provider key, Anthropic Claude or Google Gemini, and set the default model to match the provider. Without a working key the app does not error; it produces clearly fake placeholder text instead. So if output ever reads generic, or mentions the word mock, check here first. Keys are per workspace: a new workspace starts with none.

callouts.label: Rule
callouts.title: The default model must belong to the provider you gave a key for

callouts.text: Generic output, or the word 'mock', means no working key.

scenes.headline: Search is what lets it source *claims.*
scenes.narration: On the same page: a live web search key, Tavily or Serper. That is what lets the engine source claims from the real web. Without one, a flagged claim waits for you instead. Then image generation, OpenAI or Google, and vision review, which is what looks at every image before you do. Every key is pasted here, per workspace, without touching a server.

callouts.label: Live search
callouts.title: Tavily or Serper — sources every flagged claim

callouts.label: Vision review
callouts.title: Looks at every render before you do

scenes.headline: Use this app's Connect *buttons.*
scenes.narration: Step two: connect where it publishes. Settings, then Connections, shows every connection the loop needs and which are missing. Social accounts: use this app's Connect buttons, not the provider's own dashboard, or the account ends up owned by the wrong user. A mailbox, which is how invitations and digests leave. Your website, under Publish, WordPress or per-article HTML export. And analytics.

callouts.text: Connect from here, not from the provider's dashboard.

callouts.label: Mailbox
callouts.title: How invitations and digests leave the app

scenes.headline: A dash means not measured, never *zero.*
scenes.narration: Wire up measurement under Settings, then Analytics: the Search Console site and the GA4 property, with the service account granted on both. The page runs a live probe and tells you which side is missing. Until then, Measure shows dashes, and a dash means not measured, never zero.

callouts.label: Live probe
callouts.title: Tells you which side is missing

scenes.headline: Start low. Raise once you *trust it.*
scenes.narration: Then three quick dials, each covered in its own video. Set the clock: Settings, Schedule, your timezone and posting slots. Choose your gates: require approval holds every social post until an admin approves it; articles always park at review, that gate is not optional. And set the autonomy dials under Automation: articles per week, the publish day, social posts per week, and the four function modes. Start low, and raise once you trust what arrives at review.

callouts.label: Gates
callouts.title: Require approval for social; articles always park at review

callouts.label: Automation
callouts.title: Targets, publish day, four function modes

scenes.headline: Editors write. Admins *decide.*
scenes.narration: Last, invite the team under Settings, People. Editors write, draft, answer and propose. Admins approve, publish and configure. Everyone can turn the morning digest off for themselves under Notifications. That is the setup. From here the engine has a brain, places to publish, a clock, and people at the gates.

callouts.text: A brain, places to publish, a clock, and people at the gates.
